Distribution. Octavius squamatus Janák, sp. nov. is currently recorded only from the Kamberg Natural Reserve in Drakensberg Mts., KwaZulu-Natal Province, South Africa (Fig. 120). Bionomics. All specimens were collected in siftings of forest litter in a forest patch of an indigenous forest with the abundance 8.7 specimens per kg of sifted material (Fig. 132).

Distribution. Common species recorded from several countries. Verified data come from Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Ghana and Kenya.
